body:
OBSERVED 2026-08-29 against the running dev instance (cwn-local, port 8086), as a real
personal_library user with browse_global, over real HTTP.

The design (notes/MY-LIBRARY-UI-DESIGN.md) and the user-facing wiki both state that adding a book to
a shelf adds it to your library first, because you cannot shelve what you do not have. That rule is
real, but it is implemented in ONE CLIENT:

    frontend/src/components/AddToShelf.tsx:68-72
        // The shelf API correctly rejects a non-member. Establish membership
        if (!membershipReady && !(await ensureLibraryMembership())) return;

The comment is honest about it — the server rejects, and the SPA compensates. So the invariant is a
client convention, not a server invariant.

WHAT THE SERVER ACTUALLY DOES. cps/shelf.py:83 add_book_to_shelf() resolves the book through
calibre_db.common_filters(), which since #1939 carries the My Library membership predicate. A book
the account does not own is therefore not merely refused, it is INVISIBLE, and the function returns
SHELF_INVALID_BOOK. cps/api/shelves.py:229 maps that to a 404:

    POST /api/v1/shelves/8/books/223
    {"error":{"code":"not_found","message":"223 is a invalid Book Id. Could not be added to Shelf"}}

Book 223 exists, is visible to this account in the Global Library, and can be added to My Library by
the same account one call later. Telling that caller the id is invalid is wrong on the facts and
unactionable as a message.

MEASURED, same session, same user:

    seeded                          mine=51  not_in_my_library=0
    DELETE /books/223/my-library    mine=50  not_in_my_library=1  ids=[223]
    POST /shelves/8/books/223       404 'invalid Book Id'
    library afterwards              mine=50   (it did not join)
    PUT /books/223/my-library       mine=51  not_in_my_library=0  (so it was always addable)

CLASSIC IS NOT AFFECTED THE SAME WAY, stated precisely rather than assumed by parity. For a
non-owned book, classic /book/223 answers 302 and POST /shelf/add/8/223 redirects to / with no
message. So a classic user cannot normally reach the confusing error — but nor do they get the
documented behaviour, and the failure is silent rather than explained. /global-library answers 200.

SCOPE. Not data loss, and not reachable through the default SPA UI, which works around it. It
affects any non-SPA API consumer, and it means the rule the documentation states is not enforced
where rules belong. A second client — a mobile app, a script, an integration — would have to
re-implement the same workaround to match documented behaviour.

FIX SHAPE. Enforce it on the server for the user-initiated add-to-shelf paths (the API endpoint and
the classic route), so membership is established before the shelf link and the SPA's
ensureLibraryMembership() becomes redundant rather than load-bearing. Do NOT push it down into
add_book_to_shelf() unconditionally: that function is also on magic-shelf, bulk and Kobo paths where
silently granting membership would be a surprising side effect. If a path should refuse instead, it
must refuse with a message that says the book is not in the user's library — never that the id is
invalid.
title: Shelving a book you do not own is a server-side 'invalid Book Id'; the documented add-to-library-first rule lives only in the SPA client
